title: Cursor: side chats
how: ffmpeg streamed the video from its URL into cutscene's measure (256 px luma, every frame); nothing saved but these numbers and stills in scratch
whyTopTier: One idea in 17 s, told by cuts. A wide shot of the window on a painterly backdrop. A cut to one line of text at ×3.5 where two words are selected and 'Add to Side Chat' appears. A cut back wide as the side chat opens, then a cut in to its input as a question is typed.
instrument: 30 fps. The clean fit is the pan that follows the typed question: 34% of the width in 1.34 s, in-out quart (rms 0.97%; cutscene 0.3.0 1.55%).

byEye.zoom: wide ≈ 1.0 (the window about 70% of the frame); detail ≈ ×3–3.5 (one line fills the frame)
byEye.cards: 'Side Chats Available Now' (second phrase grey); the logo
byEye.cursor: native macOS I-beam and hand, native size

classify: Hand-edited feature film in the cut-not-move grammar: wide ↔ detail by hard cut. Conventions: a window on a backdrop, a single-line detail shot, a two-tone card, a spinning logo.

diagnose.observation: Framing changes only by cut: wide, ×3.5, wide, ×3, wide.
diagnose.principle: Cut-not-move: a big change of scale is a cut, so no frame is spent travelling.

diagnose.observation: The selection happens at ×3.5, where a word is a few hundred pixels wide.
diagnose.principle: Legibility at the point of action: the detail shot is sized to the smallest thing that must be read.

diagnose.observation: The frame pans with the caret at 34% of the width in 1.34 s.
diagnose.principle: A caret-follow pan on an in-out curve keeps the newest characters in frame at reading pace.

diagnose.observation: The card's second phrase is grey.
diagnose.principle: Two-tone type: the name in full weight, the status quieter.

teaches.text: Cut between wide and detail instead of moving.
Typing close-up with a pan that follows the caret.
Two-tone cards: the name in full weight, the rest grey (Cursor, v0).

critique.like: The cut to one line makes a two-word selection the entire subject of the frame.
critique.wish: In the wide shots the window is small against a busy painting, and the side chat is hard to find.
critique.wonder: Could act.select cut to ×3 on the selection's line and cut back wide when a panel opens?
